profile.reading:
This building is SLC5, one of five data centers DataBank operates on its Granite Point Campus in Bluffdale, Utah, roughly 20 miles south of Salt Lake City. DataBank's own campus materials place SLC5 at 14850 S Pony Express Road, Bluffdale, UT 84065, with 49,180 square feet of IT space and 10 megawatts of critical IT load, built to an N+1 power and N+1 cooling design; DataBank's marketing copy for this building specifically highlights positioning for high-performance computing, hyperscale cloud, content, and SaaS workloads in the Silicon Slopes region. Note that the URL slug on DataBank's own website for this building's page is mislabeled with the address of the campus's sixth building, SLC6, even though the page content itself correctly describes SLC5 and its own 14850 address; this appears to be a labeling inconsistency on DataBank's own site rather than a data conflict. DataBank acquired the underlying Granite Point site from C7 Data Centers in 2017. Across the full five-building campus, DataBank states a combined 257,770 square feet of IT space and roughly 45.9 megawatts of critical IT load on about 23 acres, fed by diverse A and B power feeds from Rocky Mountain Power in an N+1 substation configuration, with FISMA, SSAE 18, HIPAA/HITECH, PCI, and ISO 27001 compliance certifications applicable campus-wide. DataBank does not publish a specific year-opened date for SLC5. Utah's "Silicon Slopes" technology corridor has grown substantially around Salt Lake and Utah counties, drawing data center and technology employers to Bluffdale's industrial-zoned Pony Express Road corridor.

Rocky Mountain Power filed for what it described as Utah's first major large-load energy agreement under the state's 2025 large-load legislation in early February 2026, an "Operation Gigawatt" filing with the Utah Public Service Commission covering a data center customer that agreed to cover its own service costs; this filing does not name DataBank or the Granite Point campus specifically, so it is noted here only as regional grid-planning context, not as a confirmed connection to SLC5. Utah's broader "Silicon Slopes" branding effort has helped position the state as a lower-cost alternative to coastal data center markets for operators seeking reliable power and a business-friendly regulatory climate.

DataBank Ltd. was established in 2005 in a historic former Federal Reserve Bank building in downtown Dallas, Texas, that had been converted to a data center in 1999, per DataBank own corporate history page fetched this session. DataBank was acquired in July 2016 by a group of investors led by DigitalBridge, per that same page. DataBank own history page also lists a series of acquisitions expanding its footprint, three Salt Lake City area data centers from C7 Data Centers plus facilities in Cleveland and Pittsburgh from 365 Data Centers in January 2017, Lightbound, an Indianapolis based provider, in December 2018, United States and United Kingdom data center assets from zColo in December 2020, and four Houston area data centers from CyrusOne for 670 million dollars in January 2022. A trade press article fetched this session, from pe-insights.com, reports that DigitalBridge agreed to sell a 27 percent fully diluted equity stake in DataBank to Swiss Life Asset Management and EDF Invest for about 1.2 billion dollars, expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2022, reducing DigitalBridge own stake to about 15.5 percent and yielding DigitalBridge about 230 million dollars in cash proceeds. DataBank own history page states the company now operates more than 65 data centers across more than 27 markets. This row, Granite Point Campus SLC5, previously carried a two entry address array in this registry, one entry reading 14870 S Pony Express Rd with a page title fragment attached, and a second entry reading 14850 S Pony Express Rd, an internal contradiction. The operator own dedicated page for SLC5, fetched this session, despite its own URL containing the digits 14870, states the facility own address in its page text as 14850 S Pony Express Rd, Bluffdale, UT 84065, with 10 MW of critical IT load and 49,180 IT square feet. Separately, this session fetched the operator own dedicated page for a sibling row on the same campus, SLC6, whose page text gives 14870 S Pony Express Road, Bluffdale, UT 84065, the same number that had been wrongly carried in this row prior address array. This session concludes the earlier 14870 entry on this row was very likely copied in error from the SLC6 facility, corrects this row address to the single confirmed 14850 entry, and leaves the SLC6 row own separate, already correct address untouched.

reading.body:
DataBank SLC5 publishes 10 MW of IT capacity across 49,180 square feet of technical space on Pony Express Road in Bluffdale, Utah. At 10 kW per rack, a common colocation density, 10 MW supports roughly 1,000 racks; at 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, the same 10 MW supports roughly 250 racks. Those are assumptions about density, not claims from the operator. The operator does not publish a rack count, a power usage effectiveness figure, or a cooling architecture on the page retrieved.

No certifications appear in the published specifications for this facility, so no statement about what compliance tier the campus qualifies for can be made from the data.

Among the 21 facilities mapped in Utah, only 3 publish a megawatt figure, and those three together account for 39 MW of published IT capacity. SLC5's 10 MW represents roughly 26 percent of that published total, placing it second by published capacity in the state. That rank reflects only what operators have disclosed to this site, not the full installed base across Utah, most of which publishes no figure. Ten megawatts is a modest allocation by hyperscale standards, but it is a meaningful share of what is currently legible in this state.
